summary.headline: Heritage Foods Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 11,576 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.5% on procurement inflation of 8%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 10% YoY to INR 11,576 million and FY26 revenue reached INR 45,260 million. Milk procurement cost rose 8% YoY to INR 46.67 per litre (landed at chilling centre) while procurement volume fell 7% to 16.38 lakh litres per day, squeezing EBITDA to INR 522 million (4.5% margin) and PAT to INR 230 million (2.1% margin). Value-added products (VAP) grew 18% YoY in Q4 and rose to 35.5% of revenue from 32.5%. Management said cow milk flush has started in key southern regions but surplus is not yet large enough to soften procurement prices.

financial_highlights.change: FY bulk fat revenue was about INR 125 crore last year (per management, approx. 70% decline)

segments.name: Milk (liquid)
segments.commentary: Milk sales volume grew only about 1-1.2% in Q4; about 6% total milk revenue growth was mostly price-led. Company's stated target is 3-4% industry-level growth. Heritage sources about 80% cow milk, mainly south India (coastal Andhra, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra).

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: VAP revenue grew 18% YoY in Q4 (22.5% including ghee). VAP share of revenue was 35.5% in Q4 vs 32.5%; management says ghee-inclusive VAP is about 40% of revenue. Curd, paneer (30%+ growth), ghee, ice cream and buttermilk cited as drivers.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Greenfield Hyderabad (Shamirpet) plant moved into production; first-year utilisation expected at 35-40%, full utilisation in six to seven years. Acquired majority stake in Peanut Butter and Jelly Pvt Ltd (about 71% after second tranche expected in Q1/Q2 FY27); also co-manufactures for it. Ice cream prices raised about 13%.

segments.name: Bulk fats / butter
segments.commentary: Bulk fat revenue collapsed about 70% in FY26 as the company prioritised consumer business; fats segment overall down 11%. Fat business runs at about a 6% loss currently.

segments.name: North India and Mumbai regions
segments.commentary: Combined contribution still under 10% of revenue and not yet profitable; management hopes FY27 shows improvement and closeness to breakeven in at least one region.

guidance_outlook: Management expects VAP contribution to rise about 2-2.5% of revenue every year; ghee-inclusive VAP share (about 40%) expected to reach about 50% in roughly four years, maximum five.
Median EBITDA normal year about 7% (company aims to lift median to about 9%); bad year target 6.5-7%, good year above 10-11%.
Capex for FY27 expected around INR 200 crore; ongoing projects are paneer capacity expansion and a ghee project; rest is regular capex.
Milk price increases of about 4% taken in the quarter; further selective price increases taken in April and under review in May.
Management hopes FY27 may show improvement in North India and Mumbai profitability.
Management said near-term cost pressures may persist, but improving milk availability and normalising commodity dynamics are expected to help.
Q1 FY27 VAP performance described as looking 'very interesting' given good weather.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about INR 380 crore: roughly INR 300 crore on plant capacity, mainly the Hyderabad Greenfield ice cream facility and the Tirupati flavoured milk line (both inaugurated).
Curd capacity expanded by 50 tonnes per day; some buttermilk capacity added.
About INR 20 crore spent on milk chilling centre capacity additions.
Paneer volume growing upwards of 30% CAGR, implying capacity roughly doubling every two years; paneer expansion under way.
Ice cream facility first-year utilisation 35-40%; full utilisation in six to seven years assuming 20-25% annual growth.
demand_pricing: Milk price increases of about 3.96% (about 4%) in the quarter; paneer prices raised about 5%; ice cream prices about 13%; curd prices also raised. Pricing staggered by pack and region.
Management said aggressive repeated price increases muted milk volume growth; demand for VAP remained strong despite price increases.
Competition rising from national brands entering south India markets, and Heritage expanding into North and West India.
Curd penetration in south India households only about 20-25%, so 75-80% still made at home; packaged curd is substituting part of household milk demand.
Procurement price set by village-level supply/demand and competition from Hatsun Agro, Milky Mist and Aavin in Tamil Nadu; price discovery is quick and visible to all players.
Co-operatives mixed: some in AP and Telangana raised prices; Kerala and Karnataka did not (per management).
Bulk butter prices were very high in FY25, but company chose consumer business over opportunistic bulk sales in FY26.
Receivables rise attributed to higher organised trade share; management says debtors are under three weeks and from large listed entities.

qa_highlights.question: Are milk prices showing signs of moderation into May, and what does below-normal rainfall mean for milk production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cow milk flush has started and volumes are rising in cow-milk regions, but surplus is not yet enough to soften procurement prices. It declined to speculate on monsoon impact and hopes for a normal year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 capex split and what is guidance for next year?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 300 crore went into plant capacity (ice cream, flavoured milk, curd expansion), about INR 20 crore into chilling centres. FY27 capex expected around INR 200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Has milk supply constraint held back growth, and what is the pricing taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were not supply-constrained, but aggressive pricing muted milk volume growth to about 1.2%. Milk price was raised about 4% in the quarter, with further selective hikes in April and May; exact quantum for the current quarter not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth elevated and is it linked to modern trade and e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose to INR 64.81 crore at March end (INR 37.52 crore prior year), mainly MRF (INR 26 crore), which paid after 31 March. Fell to INR 51.67 crore as on 30 April; management says large listed customers, under three weeks outstanding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the milk WPI versus procurement price gap, and what drives procurement prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said WPI reported from a third-party source is not representative of its regions; NCDFI traded-value inflation is about 8%. Procurement prices are set by village-level competition and tracked closely by competitors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin structure and EBITDA aspiration, and what is the VAP path to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EBITDA about 5.9% vs about 8% prior year; median normal-year EBITDA about 7-8%, target 9%. VAP (ghee-inclusive, about 40%) expected to reach 50% in about four years.

risks_watch: Procurement price inflation (Q4 +8%) continues if cow milk flush does not build enough surplus to soften farm-gate prices.

Weather variability (below-normal rainfall outlook, El Nino risk) affecting animal productivity and fodder costs; fodder protein prices elevated since November 2025, expected to ease possibly by next month.
Milk volume growth at about 1% versus 3-4% industry target; price-led growth may be eroding volume.
Rising competition from national brands and fragmenting channels in core south India markets.
Receivables at INR 51.67 crore on 30 April vs INR 35 crore prior year close; organised trade mix rising.
Continued losses in North India and Mumbai regions and in the fats business (about 6% loss); breakeven targeted only in FY27 at best.
Execution on Shamirpet ice cream ramp-up and INR 500 crore ice cream revenue ambition by FY30 (per analyst's reference).
summary.management_tone: Cautious and measured: management acknowledges unprecedented procurement inflation and says near-term cost pressure may persist, while stressing resilience, VAP growth and early cow-flush signs. Management was evasive on specific forward pricing and monsoon impacts, declining to quantify current-quarter price increases or speculate on timing of price softening.
key_quotes: Profitability remained under pressure due to unprecedented procurement inflation.

Volume-wise, there was no constraint. We managed the volumes, right, but in terms of pricing, we had taken up pricing a little more aggressively, which might have muted the growth a little bit in terms of volumes, especially on the milk.
But it has yet to reach a place where there is sufficient surplus that the prices will start softening.

Our objective is to take the median towards a high single digit, which is about 9%. So, that in a bad year like this, our EBITDA will be around 6.5%-7%, and in a good year, we will even cross 10 % or 11%.
